children: shares decreased nearly 3.1% at 10.30 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after a federal judge refused to dismiss a proposed class action accusing the three biggest DRAM makers of restricting supply. The November 14 order by Judge Noel Wise in the Northern District of California lets the antitrust case against Micron, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix move forward. The shares had already dropped 7.62% on Monday.

As TrendForce reported on November 16, the 17 plaintiffs allege coordinated production cuts, DDR4 phase-outs and capacity restraint lifted DRAM prices as much as 500% in a year. The court rejected the argument that the case simply replays an earlier DRAM suit, though it found the shift toward high-bandwidth memory alone did not imply collusion. Defendants must answer by December 7, and a case management conference is set for January 12, 2027.

The ruling does not establish wrongdoing, and the complaint seeks no specific damages. The bigger risk is discovery, which could expose internal capacity and pricing discussions just as tight supply props up memory margins. GuruFocus gives Micron a GF Score of 96/100, reflecting elite profitability and a strong balance sheet, and sets its GF Value at $848.40. That leaves the shares at a 16% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued. The cushion is real, but litigation headlines could cap the multiple until the court defines discovery in January.

title: Micron Stocks Decrease Nearly 3.1% as Judge Lets DRAM Price-Fixing Suit Proceed
